Members need to record each instrument they play together with the
number of years played, so that coordinators can later filter by

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace tags with instruments across HiveMind
commitResults.messageBody:
Members are described by the instruments they play and for how long,
but tags could only hold free-form labels, so coordinators could not
record or filter by instrument.

Let's replace Tag with Instrument throughout:

* Person stores a set of instruments and rejects two instruments with
  the same name, ignoring case and spacing.
* add and edit accept i/INSTRUMENT:YEARS; edit keeps instruments when
  i/ is not given, replaces them when it is, and clears them on a
  bare i/.
* JSON storage saves instruments as name/years objects and rejects
  duplicate instrument names.
* filter matches whole instrument names with i/INSTRUMENT, replacing
  the temporary tag criterion until #68 adds status and minimum years.
* PersonCard, messages, sample data, test helpers, JSON fixtures, tests
  and the User Guide are updated to match.

The t/ prefix, Tag and JsonAdaptedTag are removed.

Closes #69.

commitResults.messageBody:
# Conflicts:
#	docs/UserGuide.md

Coordinators cannot recover from an accidental edit, delete or clear
without re-entering the lost information by hand.

Let's add an `undo` command that restores the member list to its state
before the most recent change. Changes made since HiveMind started can
be undone one at a time.

Following the undo/redo design proposed in the DG, a
VersionedAddressBook keeps a list of committed states and a pointer.
Commands that change data commit a new state after they succeed, so
failed commands never enter the history. States after the pointer are
kept to allow redo to be added later.

Undo history is not compared in equals(), as it is not part of the
data the user sees.

commitResults.messageTitle: Commit undo states only after a successful save
commitResults.messageBody:
Each command records its own undo state before LogicManager saves. If
the save fails, the unsaved change is still recorded, and once failed
saves are rolled back (#83) a later undo can bring the discarded change
back. Commands that change nothing, such as clearing an empty list,
also record an extra state that undo then reverts with no visible
effect.

Let's record states in LogicManager after the save succeeds, and skip
commits that do not change the data. Undo also reverts uncommitted
changes first, so the history stays consistent after a failed save.

Recording states in one place also means new commands that change
data become undoable without extra code.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document undo implementation in Developer Guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG describes undo/redo only as a proposal, in which each command
commits its own state.

Let's describe undo as implemented: LogicManager commits after a
successful save, unchanged data is not recorded, and undo reverts
uncommitted changes first. Redo stays planned.

Update and re-export the commit activity diagram and the Logic undo
sequence diagram to match. Newer PlantUML versions ignore
`skinparam ParticipantPadding` and print a warning box on sequence
diagrams, so style.puml sets the same padding with a <style> block.

A coordinator who undoes a change by mistake has to re-enter it by
hand.

Let's add a `redo` command that restores the most recently undone
change. Changes can be redone one at a time, in the order they were
undone, until a new change is made.

VersionedAddressBook already keeps undone states after the pointer, so
redo moves the pointer forward and restores that state. Redo is not
allowed while the data has uncommitted changes, as restoring a state
would silently discard them.

Update the User Guide, and the Developer Guide section that described
redo as planned.

commitResults.messageTitle: Roll back undo history when saving fails
commitResults.messageBody:
LogicManager restores the address book and filter when a command
cannot be saved, but leaves the undo history pointer where the
command moved it. A failed undo therefore leaves the history out of
step with the data: a later undo skips a state, and a later change
discards a state that should still be undoable.

Let's record the history position before each command and restore it
together with the data when saving fails.

As a failed save no longer leaves unsaved changes behind, undo no
longer needs to handle them, so let's drop that path and assert that
it does not happen.

commitResults.messageTitle: Undo and redo several changes with an optional count
commitResults.messageBody:
`undo` and `redo` ignore any argument, so `undo 3` reverts only one
change. A no-op edit after `undo` also keeps the redo history, although
the UG says any new change discards it.

Let's accept `undo [COUNT]` and `redo [COUNT]`, failing without changes
when the history is shorter than COUNT, so the user never ends up with
only part of the requested changes undone. Saving once after all steps
lets the existing rollback revert the whole command if the save fails.

Let's also make every successful data-changing command discard undone
states, letting only undo and redo opt out via Command#recordsChange().

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject unknown prefixes and invalid indexes in edit
commitResults.messageBody:
edit stores a mistyped or removed prefix inside the previous value, so
`edit 1 r/Lead t/friend` saves the role "Lead t/friend", and a capital
`S/` is read as part of the index. A zero or negative index gives only
the generic format message.

Let's reject tokens that are wrongly capitalised HiveMind prefixes or
the removed AddressBook prefixes t/ and a/, naming the token and the
accepted prefixes, and report "Index must be a positive integer." for
integer indexes that are not positive. Other slash text such as c/o
stays valid, as roles and groups may contain it.

The check lives in ArgumentTokenizer so that other parsers can reuse it.

Fixes #126
Fixes #159

A role made only of a non-breaking space is accepted and shows as a
blank role, and a role typed with repeated spaces does not match a role
filter typed with single spaces, as only ASCII whitespace is trimmed.

Let's collapse every run of ASCII or Unicode whitespace in a role to a
single space when the role is created, as groups already do, so that
blank-looking roles are rejected and stored roles compare consistently,
including roles loaded from the data file.

Fixes #131
Fixes #132

commitResults.messageBody:
The app fails to start from a folder it cannot write to: LogsCenter
logs the missing log file through its own logger before that logger is
assigned, throwing a NullPointerException. Entering only spaces shows
the help usage as an invalid command, and the edit usage shows
ty/STUDENT_OR_TEACHER while the UG shows ty/TYPE.

Let's log the file handler failure through the base logger so that the
app starts with console logging only, ignore blank input as empty input
already is, and use the UG's TYPE placeholder in the edit usage.

Fixes #136
Fixes #156
Fixes #160

commitResults.messageTitle: LogsCenter: Test the fallback when the log file cannot be opened

The file handler setup sits in LogsCenter's static initialiser, which
runs once per test run, so its failure path is never exercised by the
tests.

Let's move it into addFileHandler(Logger, String) so that the tests
can pass a log file that cannot be opened and check that a warning is
logged instead of an exception being thrown.

commitResults.messageTitle: Role: Cover all Unicode whitespace and keep old data loadable
commitResults.messageBody:
Role normalisation misses whitespace outside \s and \p{Z}, such as
U+0085, so a role made of it still looks blank. Earlier versions also
saved roles made only of characters like U+00A0, which are now invalid,
so a data file with such a role would fail to load.

Let's collapse every \p{IsWhite_Space} run, and load a stored role that
is blank only after normalisation as no role, keeping the existing
error for roles that were always blank.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow wrong-case prefix text such as A/V inside values
commitResults.messageBody:
The unknown-prefix check rejects any wrong-case HiveMind prefix that
starts a word, so values such as "Head of A/V" or "N/A" are rejected,
and it treats a tab as a word boundary although the tokenizer splits
only on spaces.

Let's flag wrong-case prefixes only before the first accepted prefix,
where they would be read as part of the preamble, flag the removed t/
and a/ only in lowercase, and start tokens only after a space.

commitResults.messageTitle: DG: Say when the undo and redo parsers read a count
UG: Mention the message when there is nothing to undo or redo
Undo, redo: Leave the requested count out of the error
commitResults.messageBody:
A count too large for an int is read as Integer.MAX_VALUE, so
`undo 99999999999` reports "Cannot undo 2147483647 changes", a number
the user never typed. The DG notes also still name canUndoAddressBook()
and canRedoAddressBook(), which the commands no longer call.

Let's report only how many changes can be undone or redone, which is
the part the user needs, and name the count methods in the DG.

commitResults.messageTitle: EditCommandParser: Handle large and full-width indexes
commitResults.messageBody:
The new index check accepts only ASCII digits, so an index typed with
full-width digits such as U+FF11, which ParserUtil.parseIndex accepts,
now gets the usage message. An index too large for an int is told it
must be a positive integer, although it is one. The parser also keeps
its own copy of the prefix list in CliSyntax.ALL_PREFIXES.

Let's accept any Unicode decimal digit, report a too-large positive
index as an invalid person index, and use CliSyntax.ALL_PREFIXES.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject removed prefixes only before the first real prefix
commitResults.messageBody:
The unknown-prefix check rejects t/ and a/ wherever they start a word,
so `edit 1 r/ a/v` and `edit 1 r/Head of a/v` fail while `edit 1 r/a/v`
passes, although all are valid free-text roles.

Let's treat t/ and a/ like wrong-case prefixes: reject them only before
the first accepted prefix, where they would otherwise become part of the
index, and keep them as text inside values.

commitResults.messageTitle: Record capitalisation-only edits in the undo history
commitResults.messageBody:
An edit that changes only the capitalisation of an instrument or group
name is saved but cannot be undone. VersionedAddressBook records a new
state only when the data differs from the current one, and it compares
with Person#equals, which ignores the case of instrument and group
names, as duplicate detection and filter matching need.

Let's compare history states with a separate exact comparison,
AddressBook#hasIdenticalData, so that every saved change is undoable
while equals keeps its case-insensitive meaning for the other features.

Fixes #178

commitResults.messageTitle: fix(import): accept UTF-8 BOM in CSV headers
commitResults.messageBody:
Excel's “CSV UTF-8” export prefixes files with a
UTF-8 byte-order mark.
Strip that leading marker before validating the
CSV header so Excel-created import files are
accepted without weakening normal header
validation.

Adds coverage for a BOM-prefixed header.

commitResults.messageTitle: fix: trim surrounding whitespace from CSV fields
commitResults.messageBody:
Normalize surrounding whitespace from imported CSV
fields before validation, matching the behavior of
 the add command and supporting values edited in
 Excel.

Whitespace-only optional fields are treated as
empty values. Add coverage for spaced CSV values
and whitespace-only groups.

commitResults.messageTitle: fix: report friendly file and instrument errors
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace raw filesystem and numeric parsing errors with import-specific messages.

Missing files now identify the requested filename and imports folder.
Invalid instrument year values now show the existing instrument format guidance instead of a Java NumberFormatException message.

Adds coverage for both error cases.

Verify that application initialization creates the
imports directory when it does not already exist.

Use a temporary import directory in MainAppTest to
avoid modifying the project’s real imports folder
during tests.

Use "person" when an import adds exactly one person, while retaining
"people" for zero or multiple imported records.

exports/current-results.csv.

member type, role, and instruments.
Values are CSV-escaped and instruments are

Save each export to the first available

commitResults.messageTitle: export: include groups in CSV output
commitResults.messageBody:
Add groups as the eighth CSV column so exported
files match the import format and retain members’
group memberships.

Groups are sorted alphabetically and serialized as
semicolon-separated values, consistent with
instruments. Empty group sets export as an empty
field.

commitResults.messageBody:
Update export expectations for the new eighth
groups column.

verifying groups are sorted and
serialized as semicolon-separated values.
Also verify members without groups
produce an empty groups field.

commitResults.messageBody:
Update the User Guide and Developer Guide to
include groups as the eighth
CSV export column.

commitResults.messageTitle: export: singular success message for one person
commitResults.messageBody:
Use “person” when exporting exactly one displayed
member, while retaining “people” for zero or
multiple exported members.

Add command-level coverage for both singular and
plural export messages.

commitResults.messageTitle: test(export): cover CSV escaping for quoted roles
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a regression test for exporting a role
containing a comma and quotation marks.

Verify that CSV quoting preserves the original
role text by escaping embedded quotes according
to the CSV format.

commitResults.messageBody: Replace the raw IOException text with an actionable message that identifies the export location and explains that it must be a writable folder. Strengthen the regression test for a file occupying the export-directory path.\n\nFixes #153

Route export through a dedicated parser so only an empty argument string is accepted. Add focused parser and integration coverage, and update the Developer Guide to reflect the parsing flow.\n\nFixes #154

Prefix exported cells that begin with =, +, -, or @ with a space so spreadsheet applications treat them as text without displaying an extra marker. Remove the prefix during import to preserve exact CSV round trips. Add codec, exporter, and importer regression coverage and document the encoding.\n\nFixes #165

Use MainApp.IMPORT_DIRECTORY as the single source
of truth for the imports folder.

This keeps application startup and the import
command aligned if the import directory changes
in the future.

Skip blank lines and rows with only empty fields
during CSV import.

to reject filenames containing invalid Windows
characters: \ / : * ? " < >
